title: Spatial nitrogen attenuation supports near‐neutral air‐water N2O exchange in the Doñana marshes (SW Spain)
content:
Abstract

We present a 2-year record (2016–2018) of dissolved N2O, CH4, and biogeochemical variables across the Doñana marshes (SW Spain). Nitrate concentrations declined by 91–98% from tidal creeks to flooded marshes, with the collapse of the nitrate/total dissolved nitrogen ratio across the salinity range being inconsistent with conservative dilution. Half the samples were N2O under-saturated and within the marsh interior N2O saturation was unrelated to salinity but associated with dissolved inorganic nitrogen, indicating biological regulation. Areal weighting of the hydrological compartments yielded an estimated air-water N2O budget of 0.8 t N yr−1 (95% CI −0.5 to 2.2), approximately 6- to 24-fold lower than reference scenarios that did not account for this spatial heterogeneity, while concurrent CH4 supersaturation dominated (≥ 96%) the CO2-equivalent emissions. The marshland thus acts as an active regulator of estuarine N2O, and budgets neglecting internal hydrological structure can severely overestimate wetland N2O emissions.
